sheet-2.description: The business centre of Glen Rock around the Erie Railroad station, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The Erie Railroad main line runs straight down the middle of the sheet with Main Street along its east side and West Main Street (marked not opened) along its west side; the frame passenger station stands between the tracks south of Rock Road. Rock Road crosses the sheet diagonally from Doremus Avenue at the west edge to Glen Avenue in the upper right. The small commercial district lies along Rock Road east of the tracks: a row of brick and frame stores numbered 194 to 204 on the south side, a drug store and a block of stores at the Glen Avenue corner on the north side, and the police station and post office in a building at the Main Street corner. West of the tracks the Smith Singer Company lumber and masons' material yard fills the block north of Rock Road with long lumber and building-material storage sheds, a woodworking shop and an auto repair garage. The block between Main Street and the railroad south of Rock Road is cut into narrow lots without buildings, ending at Bradford Street. The remaining blocks (34, 35, 41, 66, 68 and 69) hold detached frame dwellings with outbuildings: along Doremus Avenue at the west edge, on Rodney Street in the lower right, and north of Rock Road along Glen Avenue. Water pipes of six and eight inches are marked in the streets, with hydrants. Marinus Place at the bottom left is marked not opened east of Doremus Avenue.
notes: West Main Street and the east end of Marinus Place are marked not opened.
Smith Singer Co. lumber and masons' material yard west of the railroad.
Police station and post office share a building at Main Street and Rock Road.

50 ft. Business centre at the station: Rock Road, Main Street, West Main Street (not opened), Doremus Avenue, Glen Avenue, Rodney Street, Bradford Street, Marinus Place; Erie main line down the middle. One part.

sheet-3.description: The residential blocks east of the Glen Rock station, between Rock Road and the Erie Railroad's Bergen County Short Cut, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Rock Road crosses the upper left corner, where Valley Road comes in from the north; on its south side stands a row of brick stores numbered 242 to 252 ending in a bank, the eastern end of the business district drawn on sheet 2. The Bergen County Short Cut of the Erie Railroad runs diagonally from the top centre to the right edge, with Harding Plaza, a 70 ft roadway, along its north side; Harding Plaza loops around block 37, where the Municipal Building stands with the fire department, built of cinder block with a brick face. Maple Avenue runs down the right edge and crosses the railroad on a concrete bridge; south of Glen Avenue its extension is marked not opened, and the land east of it is marked no exposure beyond. The rest of the sheet is blocks 35, 36, 66 and 68 along Glen Avenue and Rodney Street, laid out in long narrow lots and built up with detached frame dwellings and garages, several of them brick veneered, and a small woodworking shop on the south side of Glen Avenue. Birchwood Road leaves Rodney Street at the bottom edge. Six- and eight-inch water pipes are marked in Rock Road, Valley Road, Glen Avenue and Rodney Street.
notes: Municipal Building with the fire department on Harding Plaza.
Maple Avenue crosses the Bergen County Short Cut on a concrete bridge; its extension south of Glen Avenue is marked not opened.
Bank at the east end of the Rock Road store row.

50 ft. Rock Road and Valley Road (top left), Glen Avenue, Rodney Street, Birchwood Road, Harding Plaza loop with the Municipal Building, Maple Avenue on a bridge over the Bergen County Short Cut. One part; few junctions (3 detected, all well spread).

sheet-4.description: Residential blocks north of Rock Road on the east side of the Erie Railroad's Bergen County Short Cut, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The railroad runs down the left edge with Valley Road beside it at the lower left. Harding Road runs from the top of the sheet south to Rock Road, where it continues as Harding Plaza; Iona Place leaves Rock Road and runs north to Hamilton Avenue, which crosses the upper part of the sheet to Maple Avenue at the right edge. Rock Road crosses the lower part of the sheet. Blocks 27, 28 (27B), 28A (29) and 30 are laid out in narrow lots and built up with detached frame dwellings and garages, a few brick veneered; the block east of Harding Road is still partly open. The brick Glen Rock Central School, with an auditorium and stage, stands alone in block 30 on Hamilton Avenue at the top right. Block 37, south of Rock Road at Maple Avenue, holds the Glen Rock Hotel (marked damaged by fire), a concrete-block auto repair garage with a showroom and gasoline tanks, an upholstering shop and stores; the public library stands on the south side of Rock Road. Abbington Terrace leaves Maple Avenue at the lower right edge. Six- and eight-inch water pipes are marked in the streets.
notes: Glen Rock Central School on Hamilton Avenue.
Glen Rock Hotel at Rock Road and Maple Avenue, marked damaged by fire.
Public library on the south side of Rock Road.
Iona Place no longer reaches Hamilton Avenue in OpenStreetMap; the junction drawn here has no modern counterpart.
Rock Road is drawn about 50 ft wide here against about 80 ft between parcels today.

50 ft. Harding Road, Iona Place, Hamilton Avenue, Rock Road, Maple Avenue, Abbington Terrace; Glen Rock Central School, Glen Rock Hotel, public library. One part; control only along Rock Road and Maple Avenue (Iona Place no longer reaches Hamilton Avenue). Rock Road drawn about 50 ft wide here (street_widths).

sheet-5.description: Residential blocks between Harding Road and Maple Avenue north of Hamilton Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Harding Road runs down the left edge and Maple Avenue down the right edge. Bedford Place and Van Allen Road (with Terrace Avenue given as its alternative name on the western stretch) cross the sheet diagonally between them, and Hamilton Avenue cuts the lower left corner; at its eastern end Van Allen Road bends north to meet Maple Avenue. Ashton Place runs north from Bedford Place at the top, and Ackerman Avenue crosses the upper right corner. Between Bedford Place and Ackerman Avenue a street labelled Oneil or Amherst is laid out across blocks 21 and 21B and marked not opened. Blocks 21, 21A, 21B, 22A, 22B, 28, 30 and 30A are divided into narrow house lots built up with detached frame dwellings and garages, a few brick veneered and several drawn from plans, with many lots still vacant toward Maple Avenue. The Glen Rock Public School, a two-storey brick building, stands in block 30 on Maple Avenue at the lower right. Water pipes of four to ten inches are marked in the streets, with hydrants.
notes: Glen Rock Public School on Maple Avenue.
The street labelled Oneil or Amherst is marked not opened; OpenStreetMap has a short Amherst Court off Maple Avenue.
Van Allen Road is also labelled Terrace Avenue on its western stretch.
Several dwellings marked as drawn from plans (under construction).

50 ft. Harding Road, Ashton Place, Bedford Place, Van Allen Road (Terrace Avenue), Hamilton Avenue, Ackerman Avenue, Oneil or Amherst (not opened), Maple Avenue; Glen Rock Public School. One part; detector found 3 junctions, Ackerman / Maple hand-picked.

sheet-6-1.description: The main part of sheet 6, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covering a long strip on both sides of the Erie Railroad north of the station. The Erie main line runs down the middle of the sheet and the Bergen County Short Cut branches off to the right toward the lower right corner. West of the main line, Doremus Avenue runs the length of the sheet with Concord Avenue and Rutland Road in the lower left; their blocks (40 and 41) are built up with detached frame dwellings, while blocks 42, 43 and 44 to the north are largely open land marked no exposure beyond, with an old grandstand and the Bergen County Coal Company's yard, concrete coal towers and a conveyor beside the tracks. Further south along the main line are the Glen Rock Coal Company, a hardware warehouse of concrete block, and part of the Smith Singer Company lumber yard. Between the two railroads, Ryan Avenue and Nassau Place are laid out but not built, and the Borden's Farm Products Company plant, a concrete-block auto and wagon storage building, stands on Broad Street (labelled Hamilton Avenue) in the upper part. East of the Short Cut, Broad Street, Harding Road, Hamilton Avenue, Van Allen Road and Bedford Place carry narrow lots with dwellings and garages (blocks 22C, 23, 31, 32, 32A, 32B, 28A). In the lower centre, Sterling Place, Austin Place, Valley Road and Glen Avenue form blocks 33, 33A, 33B and 33C reaching Rock Road at the bottom edge. Dorchester Place, marked not open, crosses the top left corner.
notes: Broad Street is labelled Broad (Hamilton) Avenue.
Borden's Farm Products Co. Inc. plant on Broad Street.
Bergen County Coal Co. and Glen Rock Coal Co. yards beside the Erie main line; an old grandstand stands in block 42.
Ryan Avenue and Nassau Place are drawn dashed (not opened); neither is in OpenStreetMap.
Dorchester Place is marked not open; it continues on part 2 of this sheet.
Sterling Place / Valley Road was rejected by the fit (14 m).

100 ft. Three parts. Part 1 (main): both sides of the Erie main line and the Bergen County Short Cut from Doremus and Concord Avenues to Harding Road, Borden's Farm Products, coal yards. Part 2 (inset, upper right): Doremus Avenue north of Dorchester Place to the Ridgewood line, Farragut, Elmore and Dorchester Places not open; placed by two points carried from part 1 along Dorchester Place (helmert, low confidence). Part 3 (inset, lower right): Concord to Doremus Avenue north of Rock Road; two hand-picked Rock Road junctions (helmert).

sheet-6-2.description: An inset in the upper right of sheet 6, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, continuing Doremus Avenue north from Dorchester Place to the boundary of the Village of Ridgewood. Doremus Avenue runs along the right side of the inset, bending toward the north-east in its upper part, and Ackerman Avenue crosses the top right corner. Three streets laid out westward from Doremus Avenue, Farragut Place, Elmore Place and Dorchester Place, are all marked not open, and the blocks between them (44A, 44B and the lower part of 44C) are divided into lots with no buildings. A few frame dwellings and garages stand on Doremus Avenue in blocks 43, 44C and 44D toward the top, and some buildings across the borough limits are labelled Ridgewood. The dash-dot borough line crosses the upper part, with a note to see the map of Ridgewood, and the western edge carries the note no exposure beyond. The inset is separated from the main part by a heavy line; Dorchester Place at its bottom edge is the same street drawn at the top left of the main part.
notes: Farragut Place, Elmore Place and Dorchester Place are marked not open; none is in OpenStreetMap under these names. Farragut Place falls about 30 m from today's Demarest Street and Leone Court junctions with Doremus Avenue.
Placed only by two points carried from part 1 along Dorchester Place.

Part 2 (inset, upper right): Doremus Avenue north of Dorchester Place to the Ridgewood line, Farragut, Elmore and Dorchester Places not open; placed by two points carried from part 1 along Dorchester Place (helmert, low confidence). sheet-6-3.description: An inset in the lower right of sheet 6, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, showing the block between Concord Avenue and Doremus Avenue on the north side of Rock Road, west of the station district. Concord Avenue runs along its left side against the heavy dividing line and Doremus Avenue along its right side; Rock Road crosses near the bottom. Block 40 is divided into house lots with a few frame dwellings and garages and two tile dwellings near Rock Road. Below Rock Road the inset shows only the outline of the next block, marked as on sheet 11.
notes: Two tile dwellings on the north side of Rock Road.
Placed by two hand-picked junctions on Rock Road only (helmert).

sheet-7.description: The northern part of Glen Rock between the Erie Railroad and Maple Avenue, up to the Ridgewood line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The Erie main line and the Bergen County Short Cut run down the left side, with Doremus Avenue beyond them at the lower left. Along the tracks stand the Ridgewood Plumbing Supply Company warehouses, a freight house, and a cannery building with its own lights and power. Broad Street (labelled Broad (Hamilton) Avenue) runs beside the railroad, with auto repair garages, an auto painting shop and a dry cleaning shed of concrete block near Ackerman Avenue. Ackerman Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from Broad Street to Maple Avenue. North of it a grid of streets, High Street, Henry, Jane, Dean, Elizabeth, Norwood Avenue, Lehigh Place, Warren Place and Clifton Place, carries blocks 13 to 20 built up with detached frame dwellings and garages, with some lots still vacant; Highwood Avenue (also labelled Park Avenue) and South Highwood Avenue run across the upper right toward Maple Avenue, where a few stores of concrete block stand. South of Ackerman Avenue, Bergen Street, Harding Road and Ashton Place run down to the bottom edge through blocks 21 to 24. The borough limits with the Village of Ridgewood run along the top and right edges, with notes to see the map of Ridgewood, and Edward Street and a short piece of High Street are drawn across the line.
notes: Jane Street is now part of Dean Street (OpenStreetMap), which also takes the drawn Dean east of Norwood Avenue.
Broad Street is labelled Broad (Hamilton) Avenue.
Ridgewood Plumbing Supply Co. warehouses beside the Erie main line.
Ackerman Avenue / Elizabeth Street was rejected by the fit (13 m).
A short street between Jane and Ackerman east of Elizabeth is marked not opened.

100 ft. North of Ackerman Avenue to the Ridgewood line: High, Henry, Jane (now Dean Street), Dean, Elizabeth, Norwood, Lehigh, Warren, Clifton, Highwood, South Highwood, Bergen, Harding, Ashton, Broad (Hamilton) Avenue, Maple Avenue. One part.

sheet-8-1.description: The north-eastern corner of Glen Rock between Maple Avenue and Prospect Street, up to the Ridgewood line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Maple Avenue runs down the left edge from Highwood or Park Avenue to Ackerman Avenue, which crosses the foot of the sheet past Central Avenue and Rockingham Place. Park Avenue rises from Maple Avenue to the Ridgewood line at the top left, with Stillwell Avenue meeting it at the borough limits. From Park Avenue, Midwood Road (also labelled Madison Road) runs diagonally across the sheet to Grove Avenue, crossed by Forest Road and Glendale Road; Beech Road ends in a turning circle west of Midwood Road, and Grove Avenue continues past a second turning circle. Prospect Street runs along the top right as the borough line, with the notes to see the map of Ridgewood beyond it. South Highwood Avenue (also labelled Highwood Avenue) crosses the lower half from Maple Avenue toward Ackerman Avenue, with Ferguson Avenue running down from it to Ackerman Avenue. The area is a newly built residential district: blocks 1 to 9 and 80 to 86 carry scattered detached frame dwellings, several of stone or brick veneer, with private garages, and many lots still empty. On Maple Avenue near Highwood Avenue stand concrete greenhouses with a store and a warehouse. Chicken coops stand in the lots along the heavy line at the right. Two areas are cut out of this part and drawn separately: a block of Park Avenue at Prospect Street (upper right) and the east side of Prospect Street south of Grove Street (right).
notes: Midwood Road is labelled Midwood Road (Madison Road).
Ferguson Avenue is now Ferguson Place (OpenStreetMap).
Stillwell is now Stillwell Place (OpenStreetMap).

The drawn junction of Forest Road and Grove Avenue is a straight crossing; the modern road has two nodes 27 m apart, so both were excluded and the junction hand-picked at the detector's position on the east node.
Concrete greenhouses on Maple Avenue at Highwood Avenue.

100 ft. Three parts. Part 1 (main): Maple Avenue to Prospect Street, Park Avenue to Ackerman Avenue (Midwood, Forest, Glendale, Grove, Beech, South Highwood, Ferguson). Part 2 (inset upper right, block 6A): Park Avenue at Prospect Street on the Ridgewood line; one junction plus a derived point (helmert, low). Part 3 (V-shaped inset right, block 95): east side of Prospect Street south of Grove Street, Belmar Spring Water Co.; two junctions (helmert, low).

sheet-8-2.description: A small inset in the upper right corner of sheet 8, enclosed by a heavy line: the block of Park Avenue at Prospect Street on the Ridgewood line, numbered block 6A, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and in the same orientation as the main map. Prospect Street runs along the top, with the notes to see the map of Ridgewood, and Park Avenue down the right side; the borough limits cut across the block on the left. The block holds five or six detached frame dwellings, one and two stories, with garages; lot numbers run along both streets and a fire hydrant stands at the corner. Water pipes of 8 inches in Prospect Street and 6 inches in Park Avenue are shown. The block lies just beyond the top edge of the main map, between Park Avenue and Prospect Street north of the Midwood Road corner, and has its own small north arrow.
notes: Placed by one hand-picked junction (Park Avenue / Prospect Street) plus a derived point along Park Avenue at the scale and rotation of the main part; low confidence.

100 ft. Three parts. Part 1 (main): Maple Avenue to Prospect Street, Park Avenue to Ackerman Avenue (Midwood, Forest, Glendale, Grove, Beech, South Highwood, Ferguson). Part 2 (inset upper right, block 6A): Park Avenue at Prospect Street on the Ridgewood line; one junction plus a derived point (helmert, low). Part 3 (V-shaped inset right, block 95): east side of Prospect Street south of Grove Street, Belmar Spring Water Co.; two junctions (helmert, low).

sheet-8-3.description: An inset on the right side of sheet 8, enclosed by a heavy V-shaped line: the east side of Prospect Street south of Grove Street, numbered block 95, drawn at 100 feet to an inch in the same orientation as the main map. Grove Street, the borough line with the Village of Ridgewood, runs along the upper arm, with South Irving Street drawn as a short stub north of it; Prospect Street runs along the lower arm from Grove Street toward the south-east. Along Prospect Street stand detached frame dwellings with garages on deep lots. At the upper right are the buildings of the Belmar Spring Water Co., a concrete block warehouse beside a spring, with a pond or stream course with an island drawn in blue below it. Further dwellings, a barn and sheds stand at the right edge. The heavy line carries the note "No exposure beyond". The area lies east of the junction of Grove and Prospect Streets shown on the main map, and is drawn displaced to the lower left of its true position.
notes: Belmar Spring Water Co. with a spring and pond.

Placed by two junctions (Grove / Prospect, detected, and Grove / South Irving, hand-picked on a short stub); helmert, low confidence. A translation of the main part's placement puts the South Irving junction about 8 m from the hand-picked position.

100 ft. Three parts. Part 1 (main): Maple Avenue to Prospect Street, Park Avenue to Ackerman Avenue (Midwood, Forest, Glendale, Grove, Beech, South Highwood, Ferguson). Part 2 (inset upper right, block 6A): Park Avenue at Prospect Street on the Ridgewood line; one junction plus a derived point (helmert, low). sheet-9.description: The central-eastern part of Glen Rock east of Maple Avenue, from Ackerman Avenue at the top to Abbington Terrace and Emerson Road at the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Maple Avenue runs down the left edge, with the ends of O'Neil or Amherst Street, Bedford Place, Van Allen Road and Terrace Avenue shown beyond it. Rock Road crosses the sheet diagonally from Maple Avenue to Ackerman Avenue at the upper right, meeting Central Avenue, Berkley Place, Grandview Place, Ridge Road and Highland Road. North of Rock Road lie Parkview Place, Carlton Place, Rockingham Place, Buckingham Place and Grandview Place, in blocks 77 to 79C; south of it Hamilton Avenue, Clinton Place, Abbington Terrace, Gramercy Place, Belmont Road and Emerson Road, in blocks 72 to 75E. The abandoned right of way of a trolley line runs from the lower centre toward the upper right, between Berkley Place and Gramercy Place. The district is residential: detached frame dwellings, a number with brick or stone veneer, with private garages, closely built along Maple Avenue and Central Avenue and more scattered to the south and east, where block 73 and block 75 are largely open. Two churches stand on Rock Road: All Saints Chapel at Central Avenue and Carlton Place, and The Community Church near Clinton Place, both heated by steam and lit by electricity. The compass rose is drawn in block 73.
notes: Grandview Place is now Devonshire Place (OpenStreetMap).
Berkley Place is spelled Berkeley Place in OpenStreetMap.
Clinton Place is labelled Clinton (Astra).
O'Neil or Amherst Street, west of Maple Avenue, is now Amherst Court.
An abandoned trolley right of way crosses blocks 73 to 75.
All Saints Chapel and The Community Church on Rock Road.
Devonshire Place / Rock Road carries a residual of about 6 m (one arm from a single edge).

100 ft. One part. East of Maple Avenue from Ackerman Avenue to Emerson Road: Rock Road, Central, Parkview, Carlton, Berkley, Rockingham, Buckingham, Grandview (now Devonshire), Highland, Ridge, Hamilton, Clinton (Astra), Abbington, Gramercy, Belmont; abandoned trolley right of way; All Saints Chapel and The Community Church.

sheet-10-1.description: The south-eastern part of Glen Rock on both sides of Ackerman Avenue, between Rock Road and Prospect Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Ackerman Avenue crosses the upper middle of the sheet from Rock Road on the left past Gramercy Place, Harristown Road, Alan Avenue and Jerome Avenue to Hillman Avenue. North of it Midwood Road, Sycamore Place, Rock Road, Gramercy Place, Harristown Road and Alan Avenue run up toward Prospect Street at the top right. South of Ackerman Avenue, Harristown Road continues to the bottom of the sheet, crossed by Highland Road, Ridge Road and Grandview Place, with Berkley Place at the lower left; Delmar Avenue and Hillman Avenue, marked not opened, run toward the lower right. The abandoned trolley right of way crosses the left side diagonally. Most of the sheet is laid out in building lots that are still empty: blocks 92, 93, 93A, 94 and 99 hold only a few detached frame dwellings, and block 99 is shown as one large open tract with the compass rose. Building is closer along Rock Road and on Jerome Avenue and the short place east of it, where a row of new one- and two-story frame dwellings with garages stands. Chicken coops and sheds stand in the back lots near Harristown Road and Grandview Place. A separate inset, enclosed by heavy lines at the lower right, shows the east end of Ackerman Avenue at Prospect Street.
notes: Sycamore Place is now Sycamore Terrace (OpenStreetMap).
Gramercy Place north of the trolley right of way is now East Gramercy Place (OpenStreetMap).
Delmar Avenue, Hillman Avenue and Berkley Place are marked not opened.
Abandoned trolley right of way across blocks 92 and 94.
Ackerman Avenue / Delmar Avenue carries a residual of about 5 m.

100 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): Ackerman Avenue between Rock Road and Hillman Avenue, Midwood, Sycamore, Gramercy, Harristown, Alan, Jerome, Prospect, Highland, Ridge, Grandview; mostly vacant lots. sheet-10-2.description: Inset 10A at the lower right of sheet 10, enclosed by heavy lines marked "No exposure beyond": the east end of Ackerman Avenue where it joins Prospect Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch in the same orientation as the main map but displaced from its true position, which lies beyond the right edge of the main map. Prospect Street runs diagonally from the upper left to the lower right, and Ackerman Avenue along the bottom, meeting it at the right edge. Between them Dolphsam Place makes a loop around block 100C, which is laid out in lots but has no buildings. North of Prospect Street, block 100D holds a few detached frame dwellings, a garage and a building marked as vacant; block 100B lies on the left. A few dwellings with garages stand south of Ackerman Avenue, outside the heavy line.
notes: Placed by one hand-picked junction (Ackerman Avenue / Prospect Street) and a derived point along Ackerman Avenue at the scale and rotation of the main part; low confidence.
Dolphsam Place could not be matched to a modern street.

sheet-11.description: The north-western part of Glen Rock between Lincoln Avenue, on the Hawthorne line, and Doremus Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points only slightly to the left, unlike the neighbouring sheets. Lincoln Avenue runs down the left edge along the borough limits of Hawthorne, with Lee Avenue and Van Winkle Avenue entering from the west and the note to see volume two of the Paterson map. Rock Road crosses the upper part of the sheet from Lincoln Avenue past North Fork, Holt (Trilby) Avenue, Henderson Street, Cedar Street, Glen Boulevard and Kent Road to Concord Avenue at the upper right; the golf course lies beyond the top edge, with the Village of Ridgewood at the top left corner. Below it Kenmore Road, Oxford Place, Hillside Avenue, Hillview Terrace, Cambridge Place, Eton Place and Decker Lane fill the lower left, and The Boulevard runs diagonally beside the brook to Oxford Place. Diamond or Bass Brook flows down the right half of the sheet, crossed by a concrete bridge on Oxford Place. East of it Concord Place (not opened), Marinus Place and Oxford Place run to Doremus Avenue, and the end of West Main Street and the Erie Railroad main line appear at the lower right. The area is a residential district of detached frame dwellings, some with brick or stone veneer, with garages, many lots still vacant; several buildings are marked "from plans". Public School No. 2, of brick with steam heat and electric lights, stands on Doremus Avenue near Marinus Place.
notes: The sheet is drawn at a rotation of about -15 degrees, against -34 to -38 on the other sheets.
Kenmore Road is now Kenmore Place (OpenStreetMap).
The south end of Glen Boulevard at Rock Road is now Spruce Place (OpenStreetMap).
Holt Avenue is labelled Holt (Trilby).
Public School No. 2 on Doremus Avenue.
Concrete bridge over Diamond or Bass Brook on Oxford Place.
Kent Road / Oxford Place was rejected (12 m); Boulevard / Marinus Place carries a residual of about 5 m.

sheet-12.description: The south-western part of Glen Rock between the Erie Railroad main line and Maple Avenue, south of Rodney Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The Erie main line runs down the left side, with West Main Street and the ends of Marinus Place and Oxford Place beyond it and Main Street along its east side. From Main Street, Bradford Street, Wilson Street and Birchwood Road (also labelled Bunce Place) run east, and Rodney Street crosses the top; Birchwood Road continues diagonally across the sheet toward the upper right. Below it a newer subdivision is laid out along Roxbury Place, Aberdeen Place, Tonawanda Road and Cumberland Road, which runs up to Maple Avenue, and further south Martens Place and Vincent Place (marked proposed), Ferndale Avenue, Catherine, Ward (Elizabeth), Lincoln (not open), Robinson Avenue and Thornbury Avenue (not open) reach the bottom edge, where the sheet is marked "No exposure beyond". Maple Avenue runs down the right side to Hanover Place and Waldron Avenue at the lower right corner. The district is residential: detached frame dwellings of one and a half and two stories with garages, fairly close along Main Street, Wilson Street, Birchwood Road and Tonawanda Road, with many vacant lots in blocks 53 to 62. East of Maple Avenue, in blocks 58 and 61, stand a few dwellings and several long chicken coops. The compass rose is drawn beside the railroad at the left.
notes: Birchwood Road is labelled Birchwood Road (Bunce Place) near Main Street.
Martens Place and Vincent Place are marked proposed; Lincoln and Thornbury Avenue are marked not open.
The detector placed Ferndale Avenue / Thornbury Avenue on the drawn Ward (Elizabeth) street; modern Thornbury Avenue appears to follow its line.
Chicken coops east of Maple Avenue.

sheet-13-1.description: The south-western corner of Glen Rock, the main part of sheet 13, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points about 27 degrees to the left. Lincoln Avenue runs down the left side along the borough limits with Hawthorne, with Rea Avenue entering from the west and the note to see volume two of the Paterson map; Decker Lane runs along the top beneath the heavy line, with the ends of Cambridge Place and Eton Place (both not opened). Grandview Avenue and Fairview Avenue cross from Lincoln Avenue to The Boulevard, which runs down the middle of the part; east of The Boulevard both are marked not opened. Blocks 50, 50A and 50B between Lincoln Avenue and The Boulevard are laid out in narrow lots, with detached frame dwellings, several with brick or stone veneer and some drawn from plans, concentrated near Lincoln Avenue and The Boulevard, and the rest vacant; a greenhouse at the top left is marked to be removed. East of The Boulevard, Diamond or Bass Brook flows south beside a long Private Lake in blocks 50C to 50E, and block 52 beyond it is open ground. The Erie Railroad main line runs down the right edge, with the end of Ferndale Avenue beyond it. Scattered dwellings beyond the bottom edge are noted but not drawn. The compass needle and scale are at the left.
notes: Drawn at a rotation of about -27 degrees, against -34 to -38 on most sheets of the atlas.
Grandview Avenue and Fairview Avenue east of The Boulevard are marked not opened; Cambridge Place and Eton Place are marked not opened.
A private lake beside Diamond or Bass Brook.
Boulevard / Fairview Avenue was hand-picked.

Part 3 (middle left): Harristown Road at Glen and Hazelhurst Avenues and the Bergen County Short Cut (helmert, low). sheet-13-2.description: The top part of sheet 13, above a heavy line marked "No exposure beyond": the southern edge of Glen Rock between Maple Avenue and Rodney Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points about 18 degrees to the right, unlike the rest of the atlas. Maple Avenue crosses the upper left corner diagonally; Waldron Avenue (not opened east of the middle) runs across the top and Harristown Road across the middle, both from Maple Avenue to Rodney Street, which runs up the right side beside the abandoned trolley right of way and is marked not opened north of Waldron Avenue. Blocks 105, 105A and 106 between the streets are laid out in narrow lots with scattered detached frame dwellings, a few of brick veneer, and many vacant lots; a woodworking shop stands at the top left near Maple Avenue. South of Harristown Road lie the upper lots of block 122 with a few dwellings and outbuildings, cut off by the heavy line; the compass rose is drawn on that line.
notes: Drawn at a rotation of about +18 degrees (north to the right of up).
Waldron Avenue east of the middle and Rodney Street north of Waldron Avenue are marked not opened.
Abandoned trolley right of way beside Rodney Street.
Rodney Street / Waldron Avenue and Harristown Road / Rodney Street were hand-picked; only four control points, all at the corners.

sheet-13-3.description: The middle-left part of sheet 13, between two heavy lines marked "No exposure beyond": Harristown Road from the abandoned trolley right of way on the left to beyond the Erie Railroad's Bergen County Short Cut, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points about 18 degrees to the right. Harristown Road runs across the part from left to right, with Glen Avenue (not opened) running north from it and Hazelhurst Avenue (not opened) south of it, just west of the railroad. The Short Cut crosses the road at the centre. North of the road lie blocks 71A and 71B, with a long concrete greenhouse and a few dwellings, and block 72C east of the railroad, with several detached frame dwellings and a barn; south of the road are blocks 121 and 122, largely vacant, with an old one-story building and a few dwellings and garages near the left. The abandoned trolley right of way crosses the left end. The area lies east of Rodney Street, south of the part above it on the page.
notes: Placed by three points along Harristown Road (Hazelhurst Avenue, Glen Avenue and the Bergen County Short Cut crossing); helmert, low confidence. Glen Avenue / Harristown Road carries a residual of about 6 m.
Glen Avenue north of Harristown Road and Hazelhurst Avenue south of it are marked not opened.
Erie Railroad Bergen County Short Cut (now the Bergen County Line) crosses Harristown Road.

sheet-13-4.description: An inset at the right of sheet 13, enclosed by heavy lines marked "No exposure beyond": Harristown Road at Berkley Place, east of the rest of the sheet and next to sheet 10, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points about 37 degrees to the right, as its own north arrow shows. Harristown Road crosses the inset from left to right, with Berkley Place (40 ft, drawn dashed as not yet opened) running north from it at the right. North of the road, block 75D holds a single dwelling 470 ft from Berkley Place, and block 76 a dwelling with garages and a concrete greenhouse. South of it, block 213 (99) holds a large concrete greenhouse range with a storage building, a few dwellings and sheds.
